What you can do today

Whiteboard items 0 to 3 are built end to end, from the database to the screen.

  • 0Tags

    Eight presets are there on first visit. Add your own with a colour, rename, or delete; deleting a tag leaves its streams untagged instead of breaking them.

  • 1Income streams

    Add, edit, and delete money that comes in on a rhythm: minimum, usual, and maximum amount, repeat every N days, a first payment date, an optional tag. Each card shows the range and the next payment.

  • 2Expense streams

    The same form and cards for money going out: rent, groceries, subscriptions.

  • 3Forecast

    Enter today's balance, pick 30, 90, or 180 days, and see the end balance at worst, expected, and best case, a chart with the range as a band, and the next eight payments in and out.

Also working: sign up, sign in, and sign out, with every /app page behind sign-in; the landing page; a top bar on desktop and a bottom tab bar on phones; an install manifest for the phone app.

How it works

Streams, not receipts

Every income and expense is a stream: a name, an optional tag, three amounts (minimum ≤ usual ≤ maximum), a repeat interval of 1 to 366 days, and a first payment date. A fixed bill such as rent puts the same number in all three. Amounts out of order are refused with a message on the field, and nothing is saved.

The forecast rule

A stream pays on firstDate + k × intervalDays for k = 0, 1, 2, and so on. Only dates inside the window count, and the math jumps straight to the first one, so a stream that started years ago costs nothing extra. Each day gets three balances:

  • Worst case: every income at its minimum, every expense at its maximum.
  • Expected: everything at its usual amount.
  • Best case: incomes at their maximum, expenses at their minimum.

Presets

The first time someone opens the app, eight tags are created for them, all in the green family so the app stays on brand:

  • Pay cheque
  • Shifts
  • Rent
  • Groceries
  • Subscriptions
  • Transport
  • Fun
  • Savings

Where the data lives

One Postgres database: tags, income streams, expense streams, and each person's starting balance, with every query limited to the signed-in person. The browser only ever talks to the SvelteKit server, which fetches from the Express API with the session cookie; that keeps the door open for an offline-capable phone app. Accounts are email and password through Better Auth.

Money is cents

Every amount is stored and sent as whole cents (110000 is $1,100.00), so nothing drifts by a fraction of a cent; the screens show dollars with two decimals in Canadian format. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and all date math runs in UTC.

The API

Every route needs the session cookie and answers 401 when signed out; bad input gets 400 naming the field that failed, and a missing row 404.

MethodPathSendGet back
GET/api/tagsnone{ tags }; creates the 8 presets on first call
POST/api/tagsname, color?201 the new tag
PATCH/api/tags/:idname?, color?the updated tag
DELETE/api/tags/:idnone204; its streams become untagged
GET/api/income-streamsnone{ streams }
POST/api/income-streamsname, tagId?, minCents, actualCents, maxCents, intervalDays, firstDate201 the new stream
PATCH/api/income-streams/:idany of the abovethe updated stream
DELETE/api/income-streams/:idnone204
Same 4/api/expense-streams[/:id]same as incomesame as income
GET/api/settingsnonestartingBalanceCents, startingDate (0 and today until set)
PUT/api/settingsstartingBalanceCents, startingDatethe saved settings
GET/api/forecast?days=90days 7 to 366one point per day (worst, expected, best), every event, the end balance

Also there: GET /api/health (open, for the deploy), GET /api/me, sign-up and sign-in under /api/auth/*, and interactive docs at /api/docs.

Next steps to plan

Items 4 to 9 from the whiteboard. Sizes are rough: S is a few hours, M most of a day, L several days.

4

Goals

M
In the model
A goals table: name, target amount in cents, start date, end date. The forecast answers one question per goal: at the end date, is the balance above the target in the worst, expected, and best case?
On screen
A goal card on the overview (“Expected: $4,470 by Dec 25, $470 over your $4,000 goal”) and a target line on the chart, plus a small list to add and edit goals.
Smallest demo
One goal, set on the overview, drawn as a line on the chart with a met or short-by sentence for each case.
5

Mobile app (PWA)

S
In the model
Nothing new. The install manifest and SVG icon already ship; missing are a service worker and PNG icons, which iPhone home screens need.
On screen
Installs to the home screen and opens full screen on the overview with the bottom tab bar; the last forecast stays readable offline, marked as possibly out of date.
Smallest demo
Open the live URL on a phone, add it to the home screen, and launch it like any other app.
6

One-time expenses

S
In the model
Either a “just once” flag on streams (the first date is the date, the interval is ignored) or a small table of dated items with the same minimum, usual, and maximum. The forecast adds each one on its day.
On screen
A “Just once” checkbox on the expense form that hides the repeat field; the card reads “Once, on Nov 14”.
Smallest demo
Add “Concert tickets, $90 to $120, Nov 14” and watch the dip appear in the band.
7

One-time incomes

S
In the model
The same mechanics as item 6 on the income side; built together, it comes nearly free.
On screen
The same checkbox on the income form; the Coming up list shows the payment once.
Smallest demo
Add “Tax refund, $300 to $500, Oct 20” and watch the expected line step up.
8

Suggestions to meet a goal

M
In the model
No new tables, but it needs goals first. A service works out the gap at the goal date and tries levers against the streams: more occurrences of an income, an expense closer to its minimum, a later end date.
On screen
Two or three plain sentences under the goal card: “Two more café shifts”, “Groceries at $280 instead of $360 closes $560 by Dec 25”.
Smallest demo
Rules only: the gap divided by the biggest income's usual amount gives the extra shifts; each expense's usual minus its minimum shows what trimming it saves.
9

Subscription reminders

S, then L
In the model
Manual first: a subscription flag and a reminder lead time on an expense stream. Later, bank or provider connections that spot recurring charges and fill in streams, a project of its own (accounts, consent, syncing).
On screen
“Renews in 3 days: Phone and subscriptions, $80” on the overview; a notification on the phone once the PWA can receive them.
Smallest demo
Flag an expense as a subscription and see a renewal strip on the overview.

Open questions for the two of you

  • Does a goal belong to the whole balance or to a tag? The whole balance matches today's forecast and is simplest; a tag such as Savings means money has to be set aside for it.
  • Do one-time items need their own screen, or is a “Just once” checkbox on the existing income and expense forms enough?
  • Are manual subscription reminders a flag on an expense stream, and should they remind inside the app only, or by notification, which waits on the phone app?
